text: Flexible endoscopy aids diagnosis of small animal gastrointestinal (GI) diseases but demands careful technique for meaningful results. This review addresses diagnostic utility, technical considerations for biopsy, optimal instrumentation for mucosal specimen collection, correlation of endoscopic indices with clinical activity and histopathology, and new diagnostic developments. Recent studies established guidelines for the optimal number and quality of biopsy specimens from different gut regions, demonstrated the value of ileal biopsy in diagnosing canine and feline chronic enteropathies, and showed that endoscopic biopsy specimens support analyses beyond routine hematoxylin and eosin histopathology, extending to immunohistochemical, microbiological, and molecular studies.
